campus: University of British Columbia — Vancouver campus
attribution: Building outlines and paths © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)

landmarks.name: Buchanan Tower
facts: It was built in 1972, a 1970s high-rise named after a former university president, like the arts building beside it.

landmarks.name: Asian Centre
facts: Its roof is shaped like a traditional pagoda, and it holds one of North America's largest research libraries in Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
It was built with steel girders from Japan's pavilion at the 1970 Osaka Expo.

landmarks.name: Old Auditorium
facts: It is a concert hall used by the School of Music and the opera program.
It opened in 1925, one of the first buildings on the Point Grey campus.

landmarks.name: Museum of Anthropology
facts: It holds close to 50,000 ethnographic objects and about 535,000 archaeological objects.
Its building, designed by Arthur Erickson, opened in 1976; the collection began with the purchase of the Frank Burnett Collection in 1927.

landmarks.name: Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Winter Sports Centre
facts: It is home to the university's men's and women's ice hockey teams.
It was built around an older rink, the historic Father Bauer Arena, which opened in October 1963.

landmarks.name: Irving K. Barber Learning Centre
facts: Students call it IKB; it is a four-storey building with library collections and study space.
It is built around the refurbished core of the university's 1925 Main Library.

landmarks.name: War Memorial Gym
facts: It is home to the university's basketball and volleyball teams.
It was dedicated on October 26, 1951, to the families of service members who died in the two world wars.

landmarks.name: Allard School of Law
landmarks.wikipedia: Peter A. Allard School of Law
facts: Its law school was renamed in 2015 after a $30 million gift from an alumnus.
The law school started in army huts after the Second World War; its first permanent building came in 1951 and was replaced in 2009.

landmarks.name: Walter C. Koerner Library
facts: It holds the main humanities and social sciences collection.
It was designed by Arthur Erickson and opened in 1997.

landmarks.name: Brock Commons - Tallwood House
facts: It is an 18-storey student residence built mostly of wood.
When it opened, it was the tallest mass timber structure in the world.

landmarks.name: Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery
landmarks.wikipedia: Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery
facts: It houses the university's collection of contemporary art.
Its building, designed by Peter Cardew, opened in 1995 and won a gold medal from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada in 2012.

landmarks.name: Beaty Biodiversity Museum
facts: Its natural history collections fill 20,000 square feet of exhibit space, including a huge blue whale skeleton.
It opened to the public on October 16, 2010, in a building designed by Patkau Architects.

landmarks.name: Life Building
facts: It was the student union building before the newer student union opened in 2015.

landmarks.name: P. A. Woodward Instructional Resources Centre
Brock Hall
facts: Its art collection was started in the 1950s to decorate the walls of the then-new building, under artist B.C. Binning.

landmarks.name: Djavad Mowafaghian Centre for Brain Health
Henry Angus Building
facts: It is the home of the business school.
A major renovation in 2012 added 55,000 square feet to the original building.

landmarks.name: Student Recreation Centre
facts: It is home to intramural sports for students.

landmarks.name: Wesbrook Building
facts: It is named after the university's first president, like a nearby mall and village.

landmarks.name: UBC Archives & UBC Rare Books and Special Collections
Woodward Library
facts: It has the largest biomedical collection in Western Canada.

landmarks.name: First Nations Longhouse
facts: It is a gathering place for Indigenous students, built in a Coast Salish style, with a library next door.

landmarks.name: School of Population and Public Health
